title: The Garden of Earthly Delights
source: Museo del Prado, Madrid (public domain). Full open triptych, full resolution, from Wikimedia Commons: The_Garden_of_earthly_delights.jpg
caption: Paradise, a garden of pleasure and a Hell full of musical instruments. Bosch packed more strange details into one triptych than most painters did in a lifetime. Which one would you zoom into? #art #arthistory #painting #history #oilpainting

slides.headline: Someone painted sheet music on a man's backside. Around 1500.
slides.sub: Hieronymus Bosch, The Garden of Earthly Delights

slides.headline: Left: Paradise
slides.text: God presents Eve to Adam. Further up the panel walk exotic animals, including a giraffe and an elephant most Europeans had never seen.

slides.headline: Centre: a garden of pleasure
slides.text: Hundreds of naked figures play, eat and embrace. Is it a warning, or a world without sin? Scholars still disagree.

slides.headline: Giant fruit everywhere
slides.text: Oversized strawberries and berries are often read as symbols of pleasure that is sweet and over in a moment.

slides.headline: Right: Hell
slides.text: Dark, frozen and burning at once. Here, the pleasures of the middle panel turn into punishments.

slides.headline: Music as torture
slides.text: A man is stretched across the strings of a harp, others are trapped inside a lute and a hurdy-gurdy.

slides.headline: The famous detail
slides.text: Sheet music is painted on a sinner's backside. In 2014 someone transcribed it and played it. It went viral as the 500-year-old butt song.

slides.headline: The Tree Man
slides.text: A hollow body standing on two boats, with a tavern inside. Some think the face looking back at us is Bosch himself.

slides.headline: The bird-headed prince
slides.text: A blue bird-headed monster sits on a high chair, swallowing sinners and dropping them into a pit below.
